audience.programmeDescription: Leiden studies religion through traditions, texts, objects and social life. The first year covers Islam, Hindu religions, Christianity and ancient religions, with source analysis and qualitative research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The revised first year and a 30 EC elective space are confirmed. This record lists 90 EC. The remaining requirements and progression into the thesis for September 2026 entrants still need confirmation before a full comparison can be assessed.

curriculum.limitation: This record shows 90 EC: the revised first-year 60 EC plus 30 EC of open study. The later-year credit table, restricted choices and complete pathway to the thesis remain unconfirmed for this intake.

componentNotes.rel1-01: Introduces religious studies as an interdisciplinary field, with historical, social and philosophical approaches to religious practices and meanings.
componentNotes.rel1-02: Studies Islam from its historical foundations to modern expressions, including texts, ritual, law, art, Sufism and political movements. The course is a prerequisite for advanced Islam study; individual advanced courses may have further rules.
componentNotes.rel1-03: Develops textual and visual source criticism, interpretation and academic research writing. Passing this course is required for positive first-year study advice and before Qualitative Research.
componentNotes.rel1-04: Studies religion as diverse symbolic behaviour across human history. The full-time first-year study-advice threshold is 45 EC, with Source-Based Research and Religion in the World both passed.
componentNotes.rel1-05: Studies diverse Hindu traditions, including historical development, ritual, mythology, philosophy, devotion, pilgrimage and modern communities.
componentNotes.rel1-06: Studies digital humanities through media, data and AI, with practical assignments and a portfolio.
componentNotes.rel1-07: Studies Christianity’s historical diversity, beliefs, churches, rituals and social and cultural contexts.
componentNotes.rel1-08: Studies religious diversity and interaction in the ancient Mediterranean and surrounding regions through texts, material sources and historical methods.
componentNotes.rel1-09: Studies lived religion through ritual, texts, objects, images, sound and bodies, with critical reading and an ethnography-based essay.
componentNotes.rel1-10: Develops research with living religious communities through participant observation, interviews, field notes and an ethnographic report. Entry requires passing Source-Based Research.
componentNotes.rel-open-study: The degree reserves 30 EC for open study. An individual package needs approval and sufficient level: normally no more than 10 EC at introductory level and at least 10 EC at advanced level. Recognised 30 EC minors at Leiden, Delft or Erasmus have an approval exemption. Courses must not overlap compulsory study; Honours courses cannot count. The Religion in a Changing World minor is excluded. For the minor Islam: Religion and Society, replace its introductory Islam course with a permitted choice that has not already counted as advanced study or another course in that minor. Internship and study-abroad plans remain subject to approval and eligibility.
